- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer playbook. In particular, it attempts to:

- use two **unauthorised fallbacks**—a 20% general cap and 18-month claim period;
- materially increase the thresholds and convert the basket into a deductible;
- subject title and capacity claims to the general limitations;
- extend limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to every type of claim;
- omit the mandatory fraud/deliberate misconduct carve-outs;
- obtain blanket data-room, public-register and Buyer-knowledge protections;
- defer material consent, debt repayment and security-release matters until too late; and
- treat Tax and IP as settled when they remain open.

The assertion that these positions are “FINAL”, “market standard” or agreed at principal level is not evidence of Buyer authority. No written Amelia Frost approval has been given for either the 20% cap or the 18-month period.

## Material departures and recommended pushback

### 1. General warranty cap — unauthorised fallback

**Seller position:** 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Playbook:** Start at 25%, or AUD 6 million. A 20% cap is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the relevant draft. There is no such authority.

**Pushback:**

- Restore the general Warranty Claim cap to **AUD 6 million**.
- Do not describe or treat AUD 4.8 million as agreed merely because it matches a potential fallback.
- Preserve separate liability regimes for Title/Fundamental claims, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.

### 2. Thresholds — materially worse and wrong basket structure

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- AUD 250,000 basket; and
- only the amount exceeding the basket is recoverable.

**Playbook:**

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- once the basket is exceeded, recovery is **from the first dollar**.

The Seller’s de minimis and basket are each five times the authorised levels, and its basket is a deductible rather than a tipping basket.

**Pushback:** Reinstate AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with full recovery once the aggregate threshold is exceeded. Ensure related claims or claims arising from the same facts are aggregated so they cannot be fragmented below the de minimis.

### 3. General limitation period — unauthorised fallback

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Playbook:** 24 months. Eighteen months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

**Pushback:** Restore **24 months**. A valid notice given within that period should preserve the claim, subject only to a reasonable period for commencing proceedings after notice.

### 4. Title and capacity — unacceptable general-regime treatment

**Seller position:** Apply the general cap and time limit to capacity and title warranties “for administrative simplicity”.

That would reduce recourse for failure to transfer the very asset being acquired to AUD 4.8 million and 18 months. It is commercially inappropriate for a 100% share acquisition.

**Pushback:**

- apply a **100% of purchase price cap** to Title/Fundamental claims;
- provide a period of at least **six years**;
- exclude them from the general de minimis, basket and Buyer-knowledge bar; and
- ensure the regime covers ownership, authority, valid issue, power to transfer and absence of encumbrances or third-party rights.

“Administrative simplicity” is not a sufficient basis to collapse distinct risk categories.

### 5. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct — missing mandatory carve-out

The Seller proposes that all limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims “of any nature”. That wording could purport to protect fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.

**Pushback:** Add an overriding carve-out, applying to the maximum extent enforceable, for:

- fraud;
- wilful concealment; and
- deliberate misconduct.

The carve-out must apply across all caps, thresholds, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy provisions, non-reliance language and other exclusions. This point is non-waivable under the playbook.

### 6. “All Claims” limitation language — hidden override risk

The proposal that limitations apply to every Claim unless expressly excluded is too broad. It risks sweeping into the general regime:

- purchase-price and other payment obligations;
- specific indemnities;
- Completion and post-Completion covenants;
- Title/Fundamental claims;
- Tax claims; and
- IP claims.

**Pushback:** Draft each regime affirmatively and separately. The general warranty limitations should apply only to defined **General Warranty Claims**, not to all Claims by default. Tax and IP remain open and must not be deemed resolved under the general regime.

### 7. Disclosure — reject blanket deemed disclosure

**Seller position:** Every matter contained or referred to anywhere in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed.

This does not satisfy the Buyer’s requirement for specific fair disclosure. It shifts the burden to the Buyer to identify the relevance and consequences of a potentially large body of material. “Contained or referred to” also risks incorporating chains of documents that are not clearly indexed or explained.

The data-room cut-off is stated as **22 September 2026**. Current facts and documents should be refreshed before signing and Completion.

**Pushback:**

- require disclosure that is sufficiently specific and detailed to identify the nature and scope of the relevant exception;
- require disclosures to be mapped to the relevant warranties;
- reject deemed disclosure merely because something appears in the data room, Accounts, a register or a public search;
- require a final indexed disclosure bundle and an updated disclosure letter;
- require confirmation of changes since the data-room cut-off; and
- prohibit disclosure by inference, prudent enquiry or documents merely referred to elsewhere.

The specific disclosures are useful diligence leads, but should not automatically qualify every warranty.

### 8. Buyer knowledge — blanket exclusion must be deleted

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records.

This is broader than actual knowledge and effectively converts inadequate disclosure into deemed Buyer knowledge. It also attributes the knowledge of an undefined population of advisers.

**Pushback:** Delete the clause. If a knowledge qualification is ultimately considered, it should:

- be confined to actual knowledge of specifically named individuals;
- not include constructive, imputed or “discoverable” knowledge;
- not attribute all adviser knowledge to the Buyer; and
- never apply to Title, capacity, fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct or specific indemnities.

Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers should instead refer to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.

### 9. Bluefen consent — Completion risk remains unresolved

Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue, around 30% of revenue. The disclosure confirms that neither final written consent nor evidence that its associated conditions have been satisfied is available.

“Reasonable endeavours” and treating the condition as satisfied upon delivery of a consent are inadequate. A written consent may be conditional, revocable or ineffective unless clause 11.3 conditions have been performed.

**Pushback:**

- retain Bluefen consent as a genuine condition precedent;
- require an effective written consent in an agreed form;
- require evidence that every condition to that consent has been satisfied or validly waived;
- prohibit unilateral Buyer waiver or deemed satisfaction merely on document delivery; and
- require notification of all Bluefen communications and any proposed concessions.

Any waiver or change to this protection should require express Buyer approval.

### 10. Riverlark debt and security — cannot be deferred

The facility is approximately AUD 3.2 million and remains unpaid, with no final security discharge. A release “following Completion” conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free transaction basis and leaves the acquired company exposed after ownership transfers.

**Pushback:**

- obtain a current lender payout letter;
- repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds;
- obtain effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security at Completion;
- verify relevant registrations and arrange prompt removal; and
- make satisfactory payoff and release documentation a Completion deliverable.

A post-Completion release should be accepted only with an irrevocable lender undertaking in an agreed form **and Amelia Frost’s approval**. Neither is presently established.

### 11. Employee bonuses — funds flow omission

DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 of Completion-triggered bonuses. They do not appear in the funds flow, and the position on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs is unknown.

Calling the bonuses “a matter for the Seller” is not sufficient if the legal obligation remains with the Company or cash needed to pay them is left in the business without an adjustment.

**Pushback:**

- identify the AUD 420,000 expressly in the funds flow;
- quantify all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs;
- require the Seller to fund the total amount or provide a specific price/funds-flow treatment;
- confirm who is the legal obligor and when the amounts become due; and
- prevent the liability from being silently excluded from debt or working-capital mechanics.

### 12. Ironquay IP — narrow indemnity and unverified amount

The materials indicate that transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independent confirmation that the amount is outstanding, correct or sufficient to secure the transfer. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Pushback:**

- verify the amount directly and obtain a current statement or confirmation from Ironquay;
- preserve a cure allowing payment of the verified SOW3 amount from Completion funds;
- require documentary confirmation that all relevant Project Materials and IP rights have transferred effectively;
- broaden the indemnity beyond the narrow payment amount to cover losses arising from non-payment, defective or incomplete assignment, ownership challenges and associated enforcement or remediation; and
- avoid accepting AUD 180,000 as conclusively payable or not payable until verified.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident — active investigation protections needed

The disclosure is appropriately cautious: it does not establish access, the precise affected population, a notifiable breach or a loss amount. The Buyer should not assume either that a breach occurred or that the matter is immaterial.

**Pushback:**

- require preservation of logs, emails, access records and the exported file;
- require a properly scoped investigation by appropriate technical and legal personnel;
- require regular updates and immediate notice of material developments;
- restrict communications, admissions, notifications and remediation commitments without appropriate consultation, subject to legal obligations;
- require delivery of the final investigation record; and
- preserve warranty and indemnity rights pending verified findings.

No numeric demand or assumed notification obligation should be inserted without evidence.

### 14. Sandbar renewals — investigate, but do not automatically deduct

The Seller characterises the AUD 330,000 renewals as ordinary-course operating costs, while the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Pushback:**

- examine contract terms, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods and accounting treatment;
- determine whether any amount relates to pre-Completion periods or a Seller decision outside ordinary course;
- restrict entering into, varying or renewing material arrangements before Completion without Buyer consent where appropriate; and
- do not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or deduct AUD 330,000 from price without the factual and accounting analysis.

### 15. Title evidence — DD-012 is not independent proof

The internal share register is relevant evidence, but it is not independent verification of ownership, valid issue, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:** Require a proper title package, including as applicable:

- original or replacement share certificates;
- constitution, historical allotment and transfer records;
- corporate approvals and executed transfer documents;
- independent corporate and PPSR searches;
- evidence concerning beneficial ownership, options and third-party rights;
- releases of security affecting the shares or Company assets; and
- Seller authority and solvency/capacity evidence.

The Title warranties and Completion deliverables must stand independently of DD-012.

### 16. Tax and IP remain open

The Seller’s statement that Tax and IP are “settled under the general regime” is inconsistent with the playbook.

**Pushback:** Mark both regimes expressly **open**. Do not accept:

- their automatic inclusion in the general cap, basket or time limit;
- an assumption of unlimited liability; or
- any assertion that a resolution has already been reached.

The eventual Tax, general IP warranty and specific Ironquay protections should be negotiated separately.

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale — avoid unnecessary concessions, but verify

The current materials indicate:

- the office lease contains a notification obligation, not necessarily a consent requirement; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment, but the disclosed wording does not establish that a share sale is an assignment.

We should not concede that either consent is required without reviewing the complete provisions. However, the Seller should comply with any applicable notice obligation and warrant that the transaction does not trigger termination, default, repricing or other adverse rights.

## Recommended negotiation package

1. Restore the general warranty package to **AUD 6 million / AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket / 24 months**.
2. Establish separate 100% and six-year minimum protection for Title/Fundamental claims.
3. Insert the overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
4. Limit the general claims regime to General Warranty Claims only; keep Title, Tax, IP, payment, indemnity and covenant categories separate.
5. Replace whole-data-room/public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.
6. Delete constructive and adviser-wide Buyer knowledge exclusions.
7. Make effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, a true Completion condition.
8. Require Riverlark payoff from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
9. Add the bonuses and all on-costs expressly to the funds flow or require equivalent Seller funding.
10. Verify and cure the Ironquay issue while broadening the specific indemnity.
11. Preserve evidence and impose investigation/update obligations for DD-006 without assuming a confirmed breach or loss.
12. Investigate Sandbar rather than automatically treating AUD 330,000 as Debt.
13. Require independent title and encumbrance evidence.
14. Record Tax and IP as unresolved.
15. Require a refreshed disclosure and diligence record through signing and Completion.

No Seller position should be recorded as agreed or final unless it has been approved through the Buyer’s own authority process.

- prevent the liability from being silently excluded from debt or working-capital mechanics.

### 12. Ironquay IP — narrow indemnity and unverified amount

The materials indicate that transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independent confirmation that the amount is outstanding, correct or sufficient to secure the transfer. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Pushback:**

- verify the amount directly and obtain a current statement or confirmation from Ironquay;
- preserve a cure allowing payment of the verified SOW3 amount from Completion funds;
- require documentary confirmation that all relevant Project Materials and IP rights have transferred effectively;
- broaden the indemnity beyond the narrow payment amount to cover losses arising from non-payment, defective or incomplete assignment, ownership challenges and associated enforcement or remediation; and
- avoid accepting AUD 180,000 as conclusively payable or not payable until verified.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident — active investigation protections needed

The disclosure is appropriately cautious: it does not establish access, the precise affected population, a notifiable breach or a loss amount. The Buyer should not assume either that a breach occurred or that the matter is immaterial.

**Pushback:**

- require preservation of logs, emails, access records and the exported file;
- require a properly scoped investigation by appropriate technical and legal personnel;
- require regular updates and immediate notice of material developments;
- restrict communications, admissions, notifications and remediation commitments without appropriate consultation, subject to legal obligations;
- require delivery of the final investigation record; and
- preserve warranty and indemnity rights pending verified findings.

No numeric demand or assumed notification obligation should be inserted without evidence.

### 14. Sandbar renewals — investigate, but do not automatically deduct

The Seller characterises the AUD 330,000 renewals as ordinary-course operating costs, while the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Pushback:**

- examine contract terms, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods and accounting treatment;
- determine whether any amount relates to pre-Completion periods or a Seller decision outside ordinary course;
- restrict entering into, varying or renewing material arrangements before Completion without Buyer consent where appropriate; and
- do not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or deduct AUD 330,000 from price without the factual and accounting analysis.

### 15. Title evidence — DD-012 is not independent proof

The internal share register is relevant evidence, but it is not independent verification of ownership, valid issue, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:** Require a proper title package, including as applicable:

- original or replacement share certificates;
- constitution, historical allotment and transfer records;
- corporate approvals and executed transfer documents;
- independent corporate and PPSR searches;
- evidence concerning beneficial ownership, options and third-party rights;
- releases of security affecting the shares or Company assets; and
- Seller authority and solvency/capacity evidence.

The Title warranties and Completion deliverables must stand independently of DD-012.

### 16. Tax and IP remain open

The Seller’s statement that Tax and IP are “settled under the general regime” is inconsistent with the playbook.

**Pushback:** Mark both regimes expressly **open**. Do not accept:

- their automatic inclusion in the general cap, basket or time limit;
- an assumption of unlimited liability; or
- any assertion that a resolution has already been reached.

The eventual Tax, general IP warranty and specific Ironquay protections should be negotiated separately.

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale — avoid unnecessary concessions, but verify

The current materials indicate:

- the office lease contains a notification obligation, not necessarily a consent requirement; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment, but the disclosed wording does not establish that a share sale is an assignment.

We should not concede that either consent is required without reviewing the complete provisions. However, the Seller should comply with any applicable notice obligation and warrant that the transaction does not trigger termination, default, repricing or other adverse rights.

## Recommended negotiation package

1. Restore the general warranty package to **AUD 6 million / AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket / 24 months**.
2. Establish separate 100% and six-year minimum protection for Title/Fundamental claims.
3. Insert the overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
4. Limit the general claims regime to General Warranty Claims only; keep Title, Tax, IP, payment, indemnity and covenant categories separate.
5. Replace whole-data-room/public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.
6. Delete constructive and adviser-wide Buyer knowledge exclusions.
7. Make effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, a true Completion condition.
8. Require Riverlark payoff from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
9. Add the bonuses and all on-costs expressly to the funds flow or require equivalent Seller funding.
10. Verify and cure the Ironquay issue while broadening the specific indemnity.
11. Preserve evidence and impose investigation/update obligations for DD-006 without assuming a confirmed breach or loss.
12. Investigate Sandbar rather than automatically treating AUD 330,000 as Debt.
13. Require independent title and encumbrance evidence.
14. Record Tax and IP as unresolved.
15. Require a refreshed disclosure and diligence record through signing and Completion.

No Seller position should be recorded as agreed or final unless it has been approved through the Buyer’s own authority process.
